title: API Routes
description: Understand Next.js Pages Router API Routes, how they compare to Route Handlers, and when each pattern is the right choice for your project.

data.text: API Routes live in the `pages/api/` folder and are the older way to build endpoints in Next.js. Even if you use the App Router for most of your app, API Routes are still fully supported and useful for certain scenarios.

Any file inside `pages/api/` becomes an endpoint automatically. The file path determines the URL, and a default export function handles the request. Next.js provides the `req` and `res` objects from Node.js, which feel familiar if you have used Express.

items: File path maps directly to URL: `pages/api/hello.ts` becomes `/api/hello`
Export a default function that receives `NextApiRequest` and `NextApiResponse`
Use `req.method` to branch logic by HTTP method

data.text: Here is a simple API Route that returns a list of users. It accepts both `GET` to read and `POST` to create, using the method to decide what to do.

data.title: API Route handling multiple methods

data.text: Both patterns let you build APIs, but they live in different parts of your project and use different request/response types. The choice often depends on which router your app uses and how you want to organize code.

items.title: Route Handlers
items.description: Live in `app/`, use Web `Request`/`Response`, and are colocated with pages. Best for new App Router projects.

items.title: API Routes
items.description: Live in `pages/api/`, use Node.js `req`/`res`, and work in both Pages and App Router projects.
cons: Not supported in App Router segments

data.title: Migration Path
data.text: If you are migrating from Pages Router to App Router, you can run both API Routes and Route Handlers side by side during the transition. There is no need to rewrite everything at once.
When to Use API Routes Today

Even in 2026, API Routes are not obsolete. They are useful when you need a stable, well-documented pattern, or when you maintain an existing Pages Router codebase. For brand-new App Router projects, prefer Route Handlers.

data.title: Key Takeaways
items: Route Handlers use `app/` and standard Web `Request`/`Response`
You can run both patterns in the same project during migration
New App Router projects should prefer Route Handlers
